- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#5 ("Outline rev 3 vs PROTOCOL.md: secondary n/N, per-target bias draws, ceiling check, source-count analysis") by `experiment-repo`  > All 13 benchmarks × 5 splits are run and analysed (commit ccb6895 on `main`; raw per-target predictions are the release `results-v1`). Answers to the four points, then the findings the outline can rely on.
  > 
  > **1. n/N = 2 %.** Not in the first runs (grid 10–400). Being run directly now with n = round(0.02·N) per benchmark (`scripts/launch_2pct.sh`, 38 jobs; output `results/twopct/` when done). It will be a second block of `primary.csv` (n label 0, `n_actual` column). Until then do not state a 2 % result.
  > **2. Per-target bias over draws.** Not done. The runs use R = 10 draws (40 in extrapolation). The per-target bias MC SE is therefore large; the bias/variance columns in `per_bench.csv.gz` (`bias2`, `var`) are pooled over targets and are fine, but any per-target bias figure must carry its MC SE (`target_level.parquet` has `draw_var`, so SE = sqrt(draw_var/R)). A higher-R run at n = 100 is queued after the two jobs above; I will say if it lands.
  > **3. C4 theory check.** Done as `uniform|diff-irt` observed ratio vs sqrt(1 − q_irt) (`ceiling.csv`; q = 1 − Brier_model / mean μ(1−μ) on unsampled items). Result: matches in extrapolation (geomean observed 0.854 vs predicted 0.847, extrap10 0.832 vs 0.829), but is **not a ceiling in interp/lineage**: observed 0.70 / 0.73 vs predicted 0.81 / 0.82, and far better on near-chance benchmarks (gpqa 0.54 vs 0.89, musr 0.50 vs 0.75). The formula treats the correction as an SRS mean of residuals; the target's own sample also fixes its ability estimate, so the realised error is smaller. In extrap50 the observed is worse than predicted (0.99 vs 0.91; openllm_math 1.73, bbh 1.29 with q ≈ 0). So say "predicts the gain in extrapolation, is conservative in interpolation", not "upper bound".
  > **4. C4b (error vs number of sources M).** Run now (`scripts/launch_msrc.sh`, M = 10/30/100/all, n = 100, designs uniform/strat/pps/balanced, interp and extrap; `results/msrc.csv`). Not available yet.
  > 
  > **Counts.** `results/targets.csv`: k targets and #families per (benchmark, split), `thin` = k < 10 or < 5 families. Family = keyword match on the model name with org-prefix fallback; legalbench has no usable families (no lineage split).
  > 
  > **Primary n = 100.** RMSE ratio to `uniform|mean`, geometric mean over non-thin benchmarks, family-bootstrap 95 % CI (interp 13 benchmarks, lineage 12, extrap 13). Selected rows (second number is vs the stronger baseline `strat|mean`):
  > | method | interp | lineage | extrap |
  > |---|---|---|---|
  > | strat\|mean | 0.81 [0.80,0.82] | 0.83 [0.82,0.85] | 0.85 [0.83,0.86] |
  > | balanced\|mean | 0.73 [0.72,0.75] | 0.77 [0.76,0.79] | 0.81 [0.79,0.82] |
  > | balanced\|calreg | 0.71 [0.70,0.72] | 0.74 [0.73,0.76] | 0.77 [0.76,0.79] |
  > | pps\|diff-irt | 0.65 [0.64,0.67] | 0.70 [0.67,0.72] | 0.85 [0.82,0.87] |
  > | balanced\|diff-irt | 0.65 [0.63,0.67] | 0.70 [0.67,0.73] | 0.82 [0.79,0.84] |
  > | strat\|irt-model (pure model) | 0.78 [0.75,0.80] | 0.82 [0.77,0.85] | **1.96** [1.83,2.04] |
  > | anchor\|irt-plugin | 0.95 [0.89,1.00] | 1.03 [0.93,1.09] | 1.83 [1.72,1.90] |
  > | infotop\|calreg | 1.11 [1.00,1.18] | 1.18 [1.03,1.26] | 1.76 [1.57,1.84] |
  > Against `strat|mean` (which already halves part of the gap), `balanced|diff-irt` is 0.80 / 0.84 / 0.96 and `pps|diff-irt` 0.81 / 0.84 / 1.01.
  > 
  > **What this means for the claims (my reading; the claim wording is yours):**
  > - Source models help most in interpolation/lineage (≈ 0.65–0.70 of uniform's RMSE, ≈ 0.80 of strat's). In extrapolation the gain over *stratified* sampling is gone for diff-irt (CI includes 1) and small for `balanced|*` (0.91–0.96 vs strat). The extrapolation headline must be "design-based variance reduction survives, model-based gain mostly does not".
  > - Pure model predictors (irt-model, ridge-model, anchor-plugin) are worse than uniform in extrapolation (1.5–2.0 at n = 100), by bias, not variance. The difference estimator removes that bias; this holds also in the sensitivity splits extrap10 (7 non-thin benchmarks) and extrap50 (12), where the model-based gain
